npcs/antagonists/pc---malcorvus-von-helv.title: PC - Malcorvus von Helvig
npcs/antagonists/pc---malcorvus-von-helv.content:
Malcorvus von Helvig is a powerful vampire connected to the destruction of PC - Vadim’s family.
According to PC - Aleksander, Malcorvus arranged a contract that lured Alexander and PC - Elara into a trap. Alexander was transformed into a vampire, while Elara agreed to serve Malcorvus in exchange for the life of their son.
Alexander claims that Malcorvus is capable of exerting supernatural control over other vampires. He was forced to serve under this influence before somehow breaking free.
By the time Alexander escaped and returned, Malcorvus, Elara and Vadim were gone. Alexander has been searching for them ever since.
Malcorvus’ current location is unknown.

npcs/antagonists/pc---needleberry-creatu.title: PC - Needleberry Creatures
npcs/antagonists/pc---needleberry-creatu.content:
Pale, elongated humanoid creatures responsible for the attacks upon PC - Needleberry. Although initially appearing animalistic, subsequent encounters have demonstrated that their behaviour is considerably more organised than first believed.
The creatures appear capable of coordinated movement, following commands and selecting particular targets. They do not simply kill everyone available to them, despite having demonstrated the numbers and strength necessary to cause significantly greater casualties.
A larger PC - Red-Eyed Creature appears to command them.
During the siege of PC - Belcons Manor, the party discovered that the creatures were capable of infiltrating the manor and somehow shutting down its dwarven generator without visibly damaging it. The Red-Eyed Creature later demonstrated limited speech and an understanding of revenge, identifying those who entered the creatures’ camp as enemies whose deaths were a priority.
During the final battle at PC - Belcons Manor, PC - Flint recovered fragmented memories of a containment facility containing creatures resembling those attacking Needleberry. Within these memories, Flint was addressed as a Custodian.
After awakening, Flint spoke several words in Dwarven which caused the attacking creatures to immediately stop.
The exact nature of the creatures and their connection to Flint remain unknown.
The party subsequently encountered another similar creature attacking refugees from PC - Canterbury. PC - Aleksander has identified himself as a vampire and explained that powerful vampires can exert control over lesser vampires or thralls, although the party has not yet established exactly how this relates to the creatures encountered around Needleberry.
Known vulnerabilities include sunlight, fire and harmful vitality energy.

npcs/antagonists/pc---red-eyed-creature.title: PC - Red-Eyed Creature
npcs/antagonists/pc---red-eyed-creature.content:
Red eyes in the storm

”…Persistence… unexpected…”


”…Will… still… persists…”


”…Incomplete…”


”…Custodian…”

A significantly larger and more intelligent creature that appears to command the vampiric creatures attacking PC - Needleberry. It was first seen only at a distance during the storm, its red eyes visible from a rooftop as the lesser creatures appeared to form up around it.
The party finally saw the creature clearly during the siege of PC - Belcons Manor. It is considerably larger than the others, with a hulking body of exposed muscle and sinew, powerful arms, animal-like legs and a sharp, skeletal face. It is capable of speaking broken Common and appears to understand concepts including revenge, enemies and exchange. Most unusually, it recognised  Kharad Vorn and understood its rules surrounding negotiation.
The creature identified those who had entered the creatures’ camp as enemies and described their deaths as a priority. After agreeing to an exchange with PC - Irilard Belcons, it demanded that Belcons meet it face-to-face. It then killed him almost effortlessly before attempting to reach the party.
uring the final battle at PC - Belcons Manor, PC - Flint recovered fragmented memories identifying himself as a Custodian. When Flint issued commands in Dwarven, the lesser creatures immediately stopped, although the Red-Eyed Creature eventually resisted his commands.
After killing PC - Vadim and severely injuring Dean, the creature hesitated when confronted directly by Flint.
It then declared:
“Custodian authority recognised. Fault in mission parameters. Returning Home.”
The creature abandoned the battle and disappeared.
When the party later returned to PC - The Cave, Flint concentrated upon the strange connection he felt towards the creature and determined that it had travelled north towards PC - The Stoneward Spine.
Its intended destination, the meaning of Home, and its exact relationship to Flint remain unknown.
The party is currently pursuing it north.
See Track the Creature Home.

npcs/general/pc---elara.title: PC - Elara
npcs/general/pc---elara.content:
Elara is the wife of PC - Alexander and mother of PC - Vadim.
According to Alexander, the two once travelled together as monster hunters, protecting travellers and settlements from dangerous creatures.
Their final contract led them into a trap arranged by PC - Malcorvus von Helvig. To protect Vadim, Elara agreed to serve Malcorvus in exchange for her son’s life. She was subsequently transformed and placed under the vampire’s control.
Alexander believes that Elara may still be alive. Her present location and condition are unknown.

npcs/needleberry/bromm-hartwell.title: Bromm Hartwell
npcs/needleberry/bromm-hartwell.content:
Blacksmith of PC - Needleberry

Sheltered townsfolk during the storm.
Protected the party.
Smithy became temporary refuge.

Following Dean’s departure from PC - Needleberry, Brom assumed responsibility for PC - The Bent Needle.
Before the party left, Brom gifted Flint a custom silver hook weapon and suggested they seek out the Redenten within the Stonewood Spine.

npcs/needleberry/louis.title: Louis
npcs/needleberry/louis.content: Louis is one of the servants working at PC - Belcons Manor, serving PC - Irilard Belcons and assisting with the day-to-day running of the estate. He was among the servants present when the party returned to the manor following their discovery of the creatures outside PC - Needleberry, greeting Dean when he arrived ahead of the others.

npcs/needleberry/pc---edda-voss.title: PC - Edda Voss
npcs/needleberry/pc---edda-voss.content:
Older woman and long term friend of Dean Picklepots in the town of Needleberry
Owner of the Pincushion - Needleberry general store
Taken by a creature in session 1
Died at the beginning of session 2.

npcs/needleberry/pc---irilard-belcons.title: PC - Irilard Belcons
npcs/needleberry/pc---irilard-belcons.content:
Irilard Belcons is the owner of the PC - Needleberry and much of the surrounding township of Needleberry. A former captain of the Velmoran Alliance, Belcons fought extensively during the Smoke War before eventually settling in Needleberry, where he has become one of the town’s wealthiest and most influential figures. His home, PC - Belcons Manor, sits above the township and contains an extensive collection of weapons, armour and other items acquired during the war.
Belcons led the year-and-a-half siege of PC - Aerra Ungor, a dwarven-controlled settlement formerly known as Matiel. Following its fall, he took one of the settlement’s dwarven-reinforced defensive walls as recompense and later incorporated it into his manor. His experiences during the war continue to shape the way he approaches danger, favouring preparation, strong defences and calculated decisions when the safety of Needleberry is threatened.
Following the attack on PC - Needleberry, Irilard Belcons tasked the party with investigating the creatures responsible. When they returned from discovering the creatures’ camp, Belcons encouraged them to remain at PC - Belcons Manor, believing the creatures had demonstrated enough restraint that their attacks might have some greater purpose.
When the creatures eventually attacked the manor, Belcons helped organise its defence and ensured the children brought from Needleberry were placed within his safe room. After the generator was disabled, he accompanied the party through the manor to restart it.
Once the generator was restored, Belcons disappeared into the vault and attempted to negotiate with the creatures under Kharad Vorn He admitted that he had suspected the creatures might follow the party and that their presence at the manor had allowed him to test this theory. Believing Needleberry had no hope of defeating them directly, he offered the lives of the party in exchange for the rest of the town, or at minimum its children.
The PC - Red-Eyed Creature accepted the possibility of an exchange and required Belcons to meet it face-to-face. Belcons complied, leaving the protection of the vault and approaching the creature personally.
The creature killed him.
Immediately afterwards, it charged towards the party. Before it could reach them, one of the manor’s defensive walls slammed shut between them. Dean noticed that immediately before his death, Belcons appeared to press something at his hip.

npcs/needleberry/pc---mayor-hammond.title: PC - Mayor Hammond
npcs/needleberry/pc---mayor-hammond.content:
Mayor of the town of Needleberry
A pigfolk administrator responsible for overseeing the town.
Mayor Hammond shared a strained relationship with Dean Picklepots, particularly surrounding local taxation. Following the attacks on Needlebury and Dean’s decision to leave the settlement, the two reconciled, with Hammond rescinding an outstanding taxation notice before Dean’s departure.

players/active/pc---aleksander.title: PC - Aleksander
players/active/pc---aleksander.content:
Aleksander is a heavily armoured traveller encountered by the party during their first night beyond PC - Needleberry. He was searching for PC - Vadim, whom he identified as his son after recognising the locket carried by the party.
Alexander was once a monster hunter who travelled alongside his wife, PC - Elara. According to his account, they were captured after accepting a contract that led them into a trap arranged by PC - Malcorvus von Helvig
Alexander was transformed into a vampire and held under Malcorvus’ control. He eventually escaped and now appears capable of resisting the supernatural influence exerted by greater vampires. He still requires blood, but claims that he does not kill those upon whom he feeds.
After learning of Vadim’s death, Alexander joined the party on their journey north. He is searching for Elara and Malcorvus and believes that both may still be alive.
Alexander carries a large shield and sword beneath layers of mismatched robes. During a fight with a vampire thrall, he demonstrated considerable physical strength by holding the creature in place while the others attacked it.

players/active/pc---ash.title: PC - Ash
players/active/pc---ash.content:
Ash arrived in PC - Needleberry shortly before the first attack upon PC - The Bent Needle. His presence as a Blightwarden initially drew uneasy attention from the townsfolk, although one child approached him without fear.
After one of the creatures attacked the tavern, Ash joined Dean, Flint and PC - Vadim in pursuing it through the town. His alchemist’s fire proved decisive in the resulting battle, helping destroy the creature.
Examining what remained revealed something deeply concerning to Ash. The influence of PC - The Rift appeared to linger around the creature.
While sheltering inside Bromm Hartwell’s smithy during the blizzard, Ash warned the others about the dangers of occult practices and spoke about Malach Vey. He later helped investigate the attacks, gathering supplies and following the creatures’ trail into PC - The Cave.
Inside the cave, Ash helped the party discover the creatures’ vulnerability to sunlight. Mirrors found within the upper chamber allowed shafts of light to be directed against them, weakening and blinding the creatures long enough for the party to escape.
After returning to Needleberry, Ash spoke privately with Irilard Belcons about his plan to protect the town. Although Belcons was acting upon an assumption, Ash understood that bringing the party to the Town Hall could place everyone gathered there in danger if the creatures were deliberately pursuing them.
Ash prepared part of the defence around PC - Belcons Manor, creating a line of fire across the approach that could be remotely ignited. When the creatures arrived, he activated the trap and set several of them alight before the manor was sealed.
During the battle in the generator room, Ash helped restart the dwarven machinery by opening the fuel valves and timing the final release. He also used alchemist’s fire against the creatures and repeatedly provided medical assistance to fallen members of the party.
Following Flint’s sudden malfunction, Ash examined the automaton and determined that his systems remained functional. The problem appeared to originate within Flint’s mind rather than from conventional physical damage.
When the red-eyed creature broke through the dining hall’s defences, Ash ignited the mustard gas released by the manor’s traps. The resulting fire destroyed many of the lesser creatures, though the red-eyed creature continued advancing.
After Vadim was killed and Dean was struck down, Ash noticed that the creature appeared reluctant to attack Flint. He pulled Dean behind the automaton, using Flint as protection until the creature recognised his Custodian authority and withdrew.
In the aftermath, Ash repaired damaged sections of Belcons Manor, secured the area and confirmed that the settlement’s defences had re-engaged.
Before departing Needleberry, Ash completed Hemlock, a clockwork raven familiar designed to assist him with alchemical work and combat.
Bromm later advised both Ash and Flint to seek out the Redenten within PC - The Stoneward Spine, believing their technological knowledge might prove useful.
Ash left Needleberry with Dean and Flint, accompanying them towards the Stonewood Spine.
During the party’s first night on the road, Ash helped defend several refugees from a vampire thrall. His initial attack drew the creature away from the survivors, but its retaliation knocked him unconscious. After recovering, Ash used another alchemical mixture to weaken the thrall against acid, fire and slashing weapons.
Ash later attempted to investigate Flint’s internal mechanisms. When he opened one of the automaton’s rear panels, a powerful electrical discharge threw him into a nearby tree and knocked him unconscious. The surge also warped the screwdriver he had been using.
Although Dean restored him, Ash remained severely dazed for some time afterwards. His examination did not reveal the source of Flint’s unusual behaviour.

players/active/pc---dean.title: PC - Dean
players/active/pc---dean.content:
Dean Picklepots was the owner and keeper of PC - The Bent Needle, one of the central gathering places within PC - Needleberry.
When the creatures first attacked the town, Dean joined Flint, Ash and PC - Vadim in pursuing one of them through the streets. The trail led to The Pincushion, where they found Edda Voss and her husband under attack. Although the party killed the creature, Edda was later found dying beneath the snow outside her shop. She passed away in Dean’s arms.
Dean remained closely involved in the defence of Needleberry. He helped investigate the creatures, gathered supplies from The Pincushion and followed their trail to PC - The Cave. Inside, he discovered a boarded passage that allowed the party to escape the pursuing creatures and make use of sunlight against them.
After returning to town, Dean supported Irilard Belcons’ plan to draw the creatures towards PC - Belcons Manor, though only on the condition that Needleberry’s children were first brought somewhere safe. He later addressed the gathered townsfolk, explaining that the party intended to draw the creatures away from the settlement.
During the defence of Belcons Manor, Dean repeatedly used the building and its machinery against the creatures. Within the generator room, he released coal onto several attackers, doused another in fuel and helped restart the generator by operating its pressure pump.
Dean witnessed Belcons attempt to exchange the party’s lives for the safety of Needleberry. He also noticed Belcons activate an unknown mechanism immediately before the red-eyed creature killed him.
In the battle that followed, Dean continued fighting while Flint became unresponsive. He was eventually struck down by the red-eyed creature, but survived after Ash pulled him behind Flint. The creature hesitated to attack the automaton and eventually recognised Flint’s authority before leaving.
Following the battle, Dean helped dispose of the creatures and performed a symbolic sacrifice for those killed during the attacks. While searching Belcons Manor, he also uncovered information concerning PC - The Smoke War, the Liberation of Vellor and the Night of Red Smoke at Karnholt.
Once the remaining threat appeared to have passed, Dean escorted the rescued children back into town. After learning that the Town Hall had been attacked, he helped organise a mob within The Bent Needle and returned to the cave in search of the escaped creature.
Before leaving Needleberry, Dean transferred ownership of PC - The Bent Needle to Bromm Hartwell, asking that the building be used for the benefit of the community. He held a final feast for the survivors and publicly announced his departure.
Dean also reached an understanding with Mayor Hammond, who rescinded his outstanding taxation notice. Dean nevertheless warned the mayor to treat the people of Needleberry fairly after he was gone.
Dean ultimately departed Needleberry alongside Ash and Flint. His search for Lagertha now takes him towards the PC - The Stoneward Spine, guided in part by the riddle she left behind:
“The unrestrained pursuit of knowledge knows what is unknowable.”
The journey marked the first time Dean had travelled any significant distance beyond Needleberry.
During the party’s first night on the road, Dean met PC - Aleksander, who revealed himself to be Vadim’s father. Dean helped explain how Vadim had died and assured Alexander that his son had not been alone during his final days.
When the party encountered refugees from PC - Canterbury under attack, Dean used his magic to protect and revive Ash. After the fight, he fed the survivors and directed them towards Needleberry, where the Bent Needle could provide them with shelter.
Dean later used his magic to revive Ash after a violent electrical discharge from Flint knocked him unconscious. He continues travelling north alongside Ash, Flint and Alexander.

players/active/pc---flint.title: PC - Flint
players/active/pc---flint.content:
Flint arrived in PC - Needleberry after becoming lost on the winter roads of Southern Aedryn. He was found by PC - Vadim, who recognised the approaching blizzard and guided him towards the settlement. Upon arriving, Flint received assistance from Bromm Hartwell, who repaired part of his damaged frame.
When the creatures attacked PC - The Bent Needle, Flint joined Dean, Ash and Vadim in pursuing them through the town. Together, they fought and killed one using alchemist’s fire.
During the investigation that followed, Flint displayed an unexplained connection to the creatures. When Vadim lost their trail beneath the snow, Flint unknowingly continued leading the party in the correct direction. This brought them to PC - The Cave outside Needleberry.
Inside the cave, an unseen voice referred to a Custodian shortly before the creatures awakened and attacked. Flint escaped alongside the others and helped bring down one of the creatures trapped within the upper chamber.
After returning to Needleberry, Flint initially sided with Vadim during the disagreement with Irilard Belcons. He later agreed to the party remaining together and helping draw the creatures away from the Town Hall.
During the defence of PC - Belcons Manor, Flint fought the creatures within the generator room. Although temporarily brought down, he recovered and killed one of them with his blade before helping the party escape to the fortified dining hall.
Following Belcons’ death, Flint suffered a violent malfunction. His body became unresponsive while his core began glowing red. Although his systems remained functional, something within his mind appeared to be forcing him into a shutdown state.
While unconscious, Flint experienced a series of fragmented memories. He saw a laboratory containing countless reflections of himself and an iron door asking him who he was. Other fragments showed him aboard a familiar ship, travelling alone through the wilderness and working within a containment facility filled with creatures resembling those attacking Needleberry.
Within the oldest of these fragments, a dwarven figure addressed Flint as Custodian and ordered him to deal with a hostile specimen.
Flint eventually awakened and spoke three words:
“Kadun, Barum, Vornak.”
The command caused all the creatures, including the red-eyed one, to freeze. Although the red-eyed creature later resisted further commands, it hesitated when confronted by Flint and eventually declared:
“Custodian authority recognised. Fault in mission parameters. Returning Home.”
The creature then abandoned the battle.
Flint’s exact relationship with the creatures remains unknown, but they recognised his authority and identified him as a Custodian.
When the party returned to the cave, Flint experienced further fragments showing that it had once served as a dwarven camp. By concentrating upon the connection he felt towards the escaped creature, he determined that it had travelled towards the PC - The Stoneward Spine.
Before leaving Needleberry, Bromm gifted Flint a custom-made silver hook weapon. Bromm also advised him to find the Redenten living within the mountains, believing their technology might be able to help him.
Flint departed Needleberry alongside Dean and Ash, travelling towards the Stonewood Spine in pursuit of the red-eyed creature and answers concerning his forgotten identity.
During the journey north, Flint reacted automatically when addressed with certain Dwarven commands. He declared that his obedience protocols had been disengaged, although he appeared to have little understanding of the response.
PC - Aleksander recognised similarities between Flint’s behaviour and the supernatural control exerted by powerful vampires.
Ash attempted to investigate Flint’s internal mechanisms. Opening one of Flint’s rear panels triggered a violent electrical discharge that knocked Ash unconscious and warped the tool in his hand.
Shortly afterwards, Flint stood rigidly upright, his eyes turned red and he began speaking in harsh Dwarven. The event ended as suddenly as it began, and Flint appeared to have no memory of what occurred.
The origin and purpose of these responses remain unknown.

players/former/pc---vadim.title: PC - Vadim
players/former/pc---vadim.content:
Vadim encountered Flint wandering the frozen roads of Southern Aedryn. Recognising the signs of an approaching blizzard, he led the lost automaton towards the nearby settlement of PC - Needleberry.
Shortly after their arrival, the creatures attacked PC - The Bent Needle. Vadim joined Flint, Dean and Ash in pursuing one of them through the settlement and helped defeat it outside The Pincushion.
Vadim assisted with the investigation into the attacks. When the trail from the abandoned Needleworks disappeared beneath the snow, the party continued searching until they reached PC - The Cave beyond Needleberry.
Within the cave, the party discovered numerous creatures standing motionless within an abandoned camp. After an unseen voice awakened them, Vadim narrowly escaped being overwhelmed and reached a smaller chamber where the party used sunlight to fight their pursuers.
After returning to Needleberry, Vadim openly opposed Irilard Belcons’ proposal that the party remain within PC - Belcons Manor. He accused Belcons of hiding while the townsfolk prepared to defend themselves and declared that he would rather die protecting Needleberry than survive behind the manor’s walls.
Vadim eventually agreed that the party should remain together, but only on the condition that he stay outside the manor and ensure that the creatures came for them rather than the town.
That evening, Vadim positioned himself outside as bait. When the red-eyed creature appeared among the trees, Vadim acknowledged it and ran for the manor, drawing the approaching creatures into Ash’s prepared line of fire.
Within the generator room, Vadim was one of the first party members brought down by the attacking creatures. After recovering, he killed the final creature before it could overwhelm Dean. Vadim then physically held a damaged pressure pipe closed while the party restarted the generator.
After Belcons’ death and the collapse of the dining hall’s defences, Vadim continued holding the line against the creatures while Flint remained unresponsive. When the party escaped through the manor window, the red-eyed creature pursued them with extraordinary speed. Vadim stopped alongside the others to face it.
The creature struck him with overwhelming force. Vadim was impaled and thrown aside. He showed no signs of life and did not recover.
After the battle, Vadim’s body was cremated by his companions.
Vadim died defending the people of Needleberry, having refused to abandon the town or allow others to face the creatures alone.
After leaving Needleberry, the party encountered PC - Aleksander, who identified himself as Vadim’s father after recognising Vadim’s locket.
According to Alexander, Vadim was the son of two monster hunters. His parents accepted a contract that led them into a trap arranged by PC - Malcorvus von Helvig. Alexander was transformed into a vampire, while Vadim’s mother, PC - Elara, agreed to serve Malcorvus in exchange for her son’s life.
Alexander believes that Vadim witnessed what happened to his parents before the family was separated. He had been searching for Vadim ever since escaping Malcorvus’ control.
The party told Alexander that Vadim had fought to protect Needleberry and that he had died surrounded by people who cared about him.

quests/main/completed/save-needleberry.title: Save Needleberry
quests/main/completed/save-needleberry.content:
The party was tasked by PC - Irilard Belcons with investigating the creatures responsible for the attacks upon PC - Needleberry after proving themselves capable of killing one during the first night.
Their investigation led from the abandoned Needleworks to PC - The Cave outside town, where they discovered a large group of PC - Needleberry Creatures gathered within what appeared to be an abandoned dwarven camp.
The attacks eventually followed the party to PC - Belcons Manor. With the children of Needleberry sheltered inside the manor, the party attempted to draw the creatures away from the rest of the town.
The resulting siege ended with the death of PC - Irilard Belcons and PC - Vadim, but the party survived. During the battle, PC - Flint discovered that the creatures recognised him as a Custodian. After recognising Flint’s authority, the PC - Red-Eyed Creature abandoned the battle, declaring that it was “Returning Home.”
The remaining creatures within the manor were dealt with and Needleberry survived the attacks.
The following day, however, another creature attacked the Town Hall, killing two townsfolk and abducting another. The party organised the townsfolk and returned to PC - The Cave, where they destroyed another lesser creature but found no sign of the Red-Eyed Creature.
Flint was able to sense that it had travelled north towards PC - The Stoneward Spine.
With the immediate threat to Needleberry ended, the party left the settlement behind.
Their pursuit of the escaped creature continues in Track the Creature Home.

quests/main/ongoing/track-the-creature-h.title: Track the Creature Home
quests/main/ongoing/track-the-creature-h.content:
Status: Active
During the battle at PC - Belcons Manor, PC - Flint discovered that the PC - Needleberry Creatures recognised him as a Custodian.
When confronted by Flint, the larger PC - Red-Eyed Creature recognised his authority but declared that there was a fault in its mission parameters.
“Custodian authority recognised. Fault in mission parameters. Returning Home.”
The creature then abandoned the battle and disappeared.
After the party returned to PC - The Cave, Flint concentrated upon the strange connection he had previously felt towards the creatures. He was able to determine that the Red-Eyed Creature had travelled far to the north, towards PC - The Stoneward Spine.
The creature’s destination remains unknown, as does the meaning of Home.
The party has left PC - Needleberry and begun travelling north in pursuit of the creature.

Follow the Red-Eyed Creature towards PC - The Stoneward Spine.

Current Progress
The party is travelling north along the road towards PC - Waymeet and PC - Ironwall.
The Red-Eyed Creature remains somewhere ahead of them.

session-recaps/pc---session-1.title: PC - Session 1
session-recaps/pc---session-1.content:
Session 1 - The First Night
The roads of Southern Aedryn proved unforgiving. Flint wandered the snow-covered roads for  days, unknowingly passing the same abandoned cart three times before eventually crossing paths with Vadim. Recognising the worsening weather and the signs of an approaching blizzard, Vadim led Flint towards the nearby mining town of Needleberry.
The town itself carried on much as it always had. Dean made his usual trip through the market square, collecting supplies for the evening’s stew and speaking with familiar faces throughout the township. Flint and Vadim arrived in town where the automaton found unexpected kindness when a local smith repaired part of his damaged frame.
Despite the cold, life continued as normal, and as evening settled over the town, everyone gradually found themselves making their way towards The Bent Needle. The tavern filled quickly. Travellers sought shelter from the worsening weather, miners finished another day’s work, and regulars settled in for the evening. Mayor Hammond made a brief appearance, personally delivering a revised taxation notice to Dean before leaving almost as quickly as he had arrived.
Not long afterwards, Ash arrived. The sight of a Blightwarden drew uneasy looks from many of the townsfolk, though one young child approached him with curiosity rather than fear.
There were some disagreements among the adventurers as they argued about use of different magic, which lead to an altercation with a miner. Before a riot broke out, the window burst open.
One of the miners was dragged into the night before anyone had the chance to react. Darkness consumed the tavern as the wind extinguished every candle, and panic followed almost immediately. A body soon fell from above, grey-skinned and marked by blackened veins, before the party caught their first glimpse of a slender black figure carrying a young girl into the night.
Without hesitation, the group gave chase.
Following the creature’s tracks through the snow, they arrived at The Pincushion. Inside, they discovered Edda Voss’  husband had already fallen victim to the creature. Before they could fully take in the scene, the creature ambushed Edda and left out the window. The group followed, and the creature attacked them from behind
The battle was fierce but brief. Through quick thinking, determination and a devastating strike with alchemist’s fire, the party brought the creature down.
For Ash, the battle revealed something else. A familiar presence lingered around the creature. The Rift.
As the creature collapsed, the town fell strangely quiet. For only a moment. Then a deep, unnatural growl echoed across Needleberry. It did not come from the creature lying at their feet. It came from somewhere within the town.
Links:
PC - Needleberry
PC - Blightwarden
PC - Mayor Hammond
PC - Edda Voss

session-recaps/pc---session-3.title: PC - Session 3
session-recaps/pc---session-3.content:
Having escaped the cave through the grate above, the party found themselves back beneath the open sky. Dean immediately broke into a run for Needleberry, with Flint following close behind, while Vadim and Ash made their way back at a steadier pace.
Dean and Flint headed straight for Belcons Manor, where Dean was greeted by Louis, one of Belcons’ servants, and given a moment to catch his breath. Once Vadim and Ash arrived, the party were brought inside to meet with Irilard Belcons and explain what they had discovered.
The meeting quickly became heated.
Belcons believed the behaviour of the creatures suggested something more deliberate than a simple attack. There had been enough of them to inflict far greater casualties on Needleberry, yet they had withdrawn. If the creatures were choosing their targets, gathering the entire town in one place alongside the only people who had successfully fought them could result in a massacre.
Vadim disagreed. He accused Belcons of hiding away in his manor while the people of Needleberry were left to defend themselves, eventually storming from the room and declaring that he would rather die protecting the town than survive behind Belcons’ walls. Flint followed him.
Dean remained behind. His history with Belcons gave him reason to trust his judgement, although he would only agree to the plan if the children of Needleberry could be brought to the manor and placed somewhere safe. Ash spoke with Belcons separately and came to understand his reasoning. Belcons was making an assumption, but if that assumption was correct, bringing the party to the Town Hall could place everyone gathered there in danger.
The party eventually regrouped on the slope outside the manor and discussed their options. Whatever they chose, separating would leave them with the worst of both plans. Vadim eventually agreed to stay at the manor, on the condition that he would remain outside and ensure the creatures came for them rather than the town.
The party returned to the Town Hall.
There, Dean addressed the people of Needleberry. He made no promise that everyone would survive the night, but told them that the party intended to draw the creatures away and that the town’s children would be taken somewhere safer before they did.
The children were brought back to Belcons Manor and taken into the safe room beneath the house. With them protected, the party prepared for the night ahead.
Vadim positioned himself outside the manor as bait. Ash prepared a line of fire across the approach, rigged so that it could be ignited from inside using a vial and rope. Belcons stood ready to close the manor’s second layer of defence, a massive dwarven-reinforced door capable of sealing the inner house.
Then they waited.
Hours passed after nightfall before Vadim finally noticed two red eyes watching from the tree line. More shapes were moving through the darkness, slowly approaching the manor.
Vadim looked towards them.
“I see you.”
Then he ran.
Vadim made it inside. Ash triggered the trap. Fire spread across the approach as the creatures charged through it, and two burning figures burst through the entrance just as Belcons activated the reinforced wall.
The manor was sealed.
With the creatures now outside, Belcons showed the party more of the defences he had built into his home. Traps were hidden throughout the manor, including floor mechanisms, gas dispensers and further defensive walls protecting the cellar and safe room.
He also explained the origin of the enormous dwarven wall now protecting them.
It had once stood at Aerra Ungor, a settlement known before its colonisation as Matiel. Belcons had led the siege of Aerra Ungor during the Smoke War, a siege that lasted a year and a half. When it finally fell, he took the wall as recompense and eventually incorporated it into the manor.
For a time, the defences held.
Then Belcons noticed something.
The generator had gone quiet.
The machinery powering the manor had stopped.
Belcons explained that the generator was located within the manor near the older section of the property. Without it, the safe room could not be properly opened and sealed. Whatever safety the manor offered would mean little if they could not get the generator running again.
With the children already waiting below and the creatures somewhere outside the defences, the party began planning how they were going to reach it.
And that is where we left off.

session-recaps/pc---session-4.title: PC - Session 4
session-recaps/pc---session-4.content:
With the manor sealed and the generator silent, the party were left with little choice but to leave the relative safety of the dining hall and make their way towards the generator room. After some deliberation, and a considerable amount of criticism directed towards Belcons for the generator’s positioning, the party settled on a route. Belcons attempted to defend the decision, explaining that the generator itself posed a significant danger if damaged and had deliberately been kept away from the areas of the manor he actually inhabited. This did little to stop the criticism.
The party decided to follow the rear wall of the manor, knowing that the doors connecting the nearby rooms to the main hall should provide some protection if they remained closed. Vadim made little effort to conceal himself, walking normally through the manor, while the others moved quietly behind him. Despite this, they reached the generator room without attracting the creatures.
Something was immediately wrong.
The door stood open. Velan had specifically been instructed to close it behind him.
Inside, they found the generator, a large piece of dwarven machinery made up of heavy metal components, pipes, valves and pressure systems. More importantly, it wasn’t damaged. Nothing had been torn apart or destroyed. Somehow, the generator had simply been shut down.
There was little time to consider what this meant. Belcons explained that restarting the generator quickly would require several of them working together, and the party moved into position. As Dean entered the room, however, he looked upwards and noticed three of the creatures clinging silently to the ceiling above them.
Combat immediately broke out.
Vadim was brought down quickly, with Flint following not long afterwards, but the party began using the generator room itself against the creatures. Dean proved particularly resourceful, releasing a large pile of coal onto two of them before dousing the third in fuel, while also managing to provide healing to his fallen allies. Amongst also healing numerous allies, Ash ignited the fuel, setting the creature alight.
The creatures began to fall. Ash killed one with alchemist’s fire while it remained buried amongst the coal. Flint brought down another with his blade, empowered through his exploit vulnerability. The final creature attempted to turn on Dean, only for Vadim to bring it down before it could bring him down.
With the immediate threat dealt with, the party turned their attention back to the generator. Ash opened the fuel valves and perfectly timed the final release. Dean operated the main pressure pump, while Vadim physically held a pressure pipe closed as the rapid startup placed enormous stress on the system.
The generator finally roared back to life.
With power restored, there was no reason to remain. The party and Belcons sprinted through the manor and made it back to the dining hall, the defensive doors closing behind them. Belcons immediately left for the vault, telling the party he would ensure the children were safely sealed inside.
He didn’t return.
Instead, his voice eventually reverberated through the walls.
Belcons called out to the creatures. He invoked Kharad Vorn, demanding negotiation and asking what they wanted. For some time, there was no answer. Then, for the first time, the creature with the red eyes spoke.
It recognised revenge.
It spoke of enemies previously detected within the camp.
And it identified their deaths as a priority.
Belcons then addressed the party privately. He admitted that he had suspected the creatures might follow them and that bringing them to the manor had allowed him to test that theory. Their behaviour had confirmed his suspicions. In his mind, Needleberry could not hope to defeat an organised force of creatures this powerful.
But if they could be reasoned with, perhaps the town could still be saved.
Belcons offered them an exchange: the lives of the party, who had attacked and killed their kind, in exchange for the rest of Needleberry.
The creature accepted.
But it demanded that the exchange be conducted face-to-face, in accordance with Kharad Vorn.
Belcons agreed.
A safety wall suddenly sealed the party away from the vault. They heard the vault open, footsteps beyond the wall, and then the vault sealing again. When the safety wall withdrew, they saw Belcons standing some distance away.
And, for the first time, they properly saw the creature with the red eyes.
It towered over the others, its body made from muscle and sinew, with unnaturally rounded shoulders, powerful arms and animal-like legs supporting a distinctly unnatural humanoid frame. Its hairless face was sharp and skeletal, almost resembling the shape of a goat’s skull beneath tightly stretched skin. Behind it stood nearly a dozen of the lesser creatures in perfect unison.
A visibly shaken Belcons indicated the party.
“Very well. The terms of the exchange. There they are.”
The creature extended one enormous clawed hand towards him.
Belcons hesitated, then reached forward to accept it.
The creature tore his arm from his body.
Before Belcons’ scream could finish, it tore off his head.
It crushed what remained in its hand and immediately charged towards the party.
Then the wall slammed shut.
The creature crashed against the metal on the other side, scratching and tearing furiously at the barrier as the entire manor rattled around them.
In the brief moment before his death, Dean noticed one final thing.
Belcons’ remaining hand had moved to his hip.
And just before the creature killed him, he pressed something.
The rumbling of the building as the creature attacked the wall forecast the end of the session.

session-recaps/pc---session-5.title: PC - Session 5
session-recaps/pc---session-5.content:
Following Belcons’ death, the party found themselves trapped within the dining hall as the red-eyed monstrosity hurled itself repeatedly against the dwarven steel barrier protecting them from the rest of the manor. The wall held, but only just. Each impact sent tremors through the room, and it became increasingly clear that it would not withstand the creature forever.
As the party began urgently discussing how they might survive what was coming next, Flint suddenly suffered a violent malfunction. His voice distorted, dropping into a deeper register before breaking apart into mechanical static. Moments later his entire body locked up, his core glowing an ominous red. When Ash examined him, he discovered Flint was not damaged in the conventional sense. His systems remained functional, but something inside his mind appeared to be forcing him into a catastrophic shutdown state.
With Flint completely unresponsive and the creatures steadily breaking through the barrier, the situation rapidly deteriorated. Fortunately, a familiar voice called out through the walls.
Louis had survived.
From elsewhere within the manor, Belcons’ loyal butler directed the party to a number of defensive systems hidden throughout the dining hall. With little time remaining, the party positioned themselves and prepared what traps they could. Mustard gas could be released into the centre of the room. A spear trap remained hidden within one wall. A flame trap ran through the ceiling above.
Then the steel wall finally began to fail.
A tear appeared in the metal, revealing glimpses of the enormous red-eyed creature beyond. It continued ripping apart the barrier while the first of the smaller creatures squeezed through. Combat began once again.
As the battle unfolded, Flint found himself elsewhere.
He awoke within a strange stone structure. Walking through unfamiliar corridors, he eventually entered what appeared to be a laboratory. Strange samples, biological remains and unfamiliar devices filled the room. Beneath a sheet in one corner stood a large glass chamber.
When Flint removed the sheet, he found himself staring at his own reflection.
Then dozens of reflections.
Hundreds.
Everywhere he looked, he saw himself.
The world spiralled apart around him until everything vanished.
When his vision cleared, he found himself standing before a large iron door bearing a simple question:
Who are you?
Behind him stood three doors.
Passing through the first, Flint found himself once again aboard a familiar ship. He stood amongst familiar faces as a crewman called for the ship’s Thaumaturge. He helped guide the vessel exactly as he had countless times before.
The second door led to a different chapter of his life. Alone, he travelled through the winter wilderness. For perhaps the first time in his existence, he moved without responsibility, obligation or destination, guided only by a vague feeling that he was travelling towards something he could no longer remember.
The final door led somewhere much older.
Flint found himself seated behind a desk within a laboratory office. A dwarven figure entered and calmly delivered a report.
“Custodian, specimen 12 has become hostile again, please take care of it.”
Without hesitation, Flint rose and moved into a containment facility. Reinforced chambers lined the walls. Beyond thick glass stood pale, motionless creatures remarkably similar to those attacking Needleberry.
The memory faded before he could learn more.
Back in reality, the battle worsened.
The creatures steadily poured through the breach as the red-eyed monstrosity continued tearing the wall apart. The party unleashed every trap available to them. Mustard gas filled the air and Ash ignited it with alchemical fire. Flames spread throughout the chamber while the spear trap shredded creatures unfortunate enough to advance through its path. Many of the lesser creatures were destroyed almost instantly.
The red-eyed creature continued forward, flesh melting but no signs of stopping.
As Dean, Ash and Vadim struggled to hold the line, Flint continued working through fragmented memories. Slowly, he pieced together the identity his damaged mind had buried.
After much deliberation, Flint found his designation.
Custodian.
As that understanding settled into place, something within him unlocked.
Flint awoke.
His core and eyes a deep red. He uttered 3 words ” Kadun, Barum, Vornak” and all the creatures froze, including the red-eyed one.
The party fled outside through the window in an instant, watching to see if the creatures would follow. The red-eyed creature began to twitch, before exploding forward at blinding speed, and catching up to the party.
Flint attempted the dwarven command phrases, but the creature ignored them. Whatever authority he possessed was apparently insufficient.
The enormous creature confronted the party in no time, and all members stopped to meet it.
The creature struck.
Despite his efforts, the sheer force of the attack proved overwhelming. Already weakened from earlier battles, Vadim was impaled and hurled violently aside, no signs of life. Dean was then struck down, barely stable.
A brilliant act of ingenuity from Ash saw him notice the creature’s hesitation to attack Flint, as he grabbed Dean’s body and bunkered behind Flint.
For the first time, the monstrosity hesitated.
Its glowing eyes fixed upon the automaton.
The room fell silent.
After several moments, the creature spoke.
“Custodian authority recognised. Fault in mission parameters. Returning Home”
Without another word, the monstrosity turned and departed, abandoning the battle entirely.
The party returned to the manor to find the remaining creatures standing still, as they were in the cave.
The victory came at a cost.
In the aftermath, the party dealt with the remaining creatures, ensuring none would rise again. Dean performed a symbolic sacrifice on behalf of the town’s dead before helping dispose of the remains scattered throughout the manor. Ash repaired damage to the building, secured the area and confirmed the settlement’s defences had re-engaged.
Vadim’s body was cremated.
Belcons’ remains were gathered.
And for the first time since the attack began, Needleberry finally grew quiet.
While searching Belcons Manor, Dean spent time exploring Belcons’ library and uncovered details surrounding the century-long Smoke War, including the Liberation of Vellor and the infamous Night of Red Smoke at Karnholt.
Far more troubling, however, was what the party had learned about Flint.
The creatures knew him and recognised his authority. They called him Custodian.
And now this creature was heading home, wherever that was.

session-recaps/pc---session-6.title: PC - Session 6
session-recaps/pc---session-6.content:
The party awoke the following morning within PC - Belcons Manor, having finally survived the horrors hidden beneath PC - Needleberry. With the immediate danger apparently gone, attention turned towards the children they had rescued from the vault below.
Escorting the children back to town, the party expected to find the settlement beginning to recover from the night’s events.
Instead, they found disaster waiting for them.
During the night, the town hall had come under attack. One of the vampire creatures had entered the settlement unseen, killing two townsfolk and abducting another before disappearing back into the darkness. The town was once again gripped by fear, and it quickly became apparent that although the manor had been secured, the true source of the attacks remained at large.
The party immediately began discussing what had happened.
The red-eyed creature Flint had identified as a Custodian construct had departed the previous night after declaring it was returning home. The only problem was that the party did not know where home was. Attention quickly turned towards the cave where the creatures had first been discovered.
Assuming the vampire may have returned there, the party gathered within PC - The Bent Needle and began organising a hunting expedition. Word spread rapidly throughout the settlement. Armed with torches, mirrors, weapons and determination, nearly forty villagers volunteered to accompany them into the wilderness.
Once preparations were complete, the newly formed mob set out for the cave.
The journey passed without incident, and before long the group found themselves standing once again outside the dark entrance where so much of the town’s suffering had begun. As they cautiously entered the cavern, a silhouette appeared deeper within the tunnels.
The reaction was immediate. Mirrors were raised and sunlight reflected into the darkness while alchemical fire was hurled towards the figure. The combined assault erupted into flame, engulfing the creature before it could properly react.
Within moments it was dead.
As the flames died down, however, the party realised something was wrong. The creature they had slain was not the vampire they had been hunting. It was merely one of the lesser spawn. The true creature was nowhere to be found. Unwilling to leave without answers, the party began searching the cavern more thoroughly.
While exploring the cave, Flint found himself distracted by strange impressions and fragmented images. He saw glimpses of campfires, equipment and figures moving through the cave long before it had become a vampire’s lair. The flashes were brief and incomplete, but they carried the same unsettling familiarity as many of the memories he had experienced since discovering his connection to the Custodians.
The fragments convinced him that the cave had once served as some kind of dwarven camp.
Focusing instead on the sensation that had previously connected him to the vampire, Flint attempted to determine where the creature had gone. Slowly, an answer emerged.
The feeling stretched far beyond Needleberry. Far beyond the surrounding countryside. Whatever the creature was, it had already fled towards the distant mountains known as the Stonewood Spine. Reaching it would take weeks. With little else to accomplish within the cave, the hunting party returned home.
Back in town, Dean made a decision. Having protected the settlement through its darkest period, he announced that he would be leaving Needleberry behind. His path now lay elsewhere, driven by both the vampire’s escape and the unresolved mystery surrounding a woman from his past named Lagertha.
Before departing, Dean formally handed ownership of PC - The Bent Needle to Bromm. He instructed him to use the building for the benefit of the community, whether as a shelter, gathering place or home for those left without families after the recent attacks.
That evening, the townsfolk gathered one final time within the tavern. Food was shared, drinks were poured and survivors reflected upon everything they had endured together. Dean used the occasion to publicly announce his departure and bid farewell to the settlement he had helped save.
During the celebrations, Ash finally completed work on a long-running project. His clockwork raven familiar, Hemlock, became fully operational, providing him with a capable assistant for both alchemical work and future adventures. Elsewhere, Dean spoke with Mayor Ham.
The conversation proved considerably more civil than many of their previous encounters. As a final gesture, the mayor rescinded an outstanding tax notice that had long irritated Dean. Though the two reached an understanding, Dean nevertheless made it abundantly clear that he expected the town to be treated fairly after he was gone.
Before the party departed, Bromm presented Flint with a custom-made silver hook weapon. During their conversation, he suggested they seek out the Redenten within the Stonewood Spine, claiming the ratfolk possessed knowledge and skills that might prove useful to both Flint and Ash.
The following morning, the party finally left Needleberry behind. Their departure was aided by the acquisition of a horse and cart, which Dean somehow managed to secure after a thoroughly confusing interaction with a visually impaired stablehand. As the settlement faded into the distance behind them, Dean shared the final clue Lagertha had left in his possession.
“The unrestrained pursuit of knowledge knows what is unknowable.”
None of them understood its meaning. With Flint’s past, the escaped vampire and Lagertha’s riddle all pointing towards the same destination, the party travelled towards the Ironwall trade route and the distant peaks of the Stonewood Spine. For the first time since arriving in Needleberry, the road lay open before them once more.

session-recaps/pc---session-7.title: PC - Session 7
session-recaps/pc---session-7.content:
For the first time since arriving in Needleberry, the party found themselves beyond the borders of the settlement. The road north stretched ahead through the winter wilderness, partially buried beneath fresh snow. Forests crowded either side of the path, their branches heavy with white, while the distant peaks of the Stonewood Spine remained somewhere beyond the horizon.
For Dean, this was the furthest he had ever travelled from home. Although he knew the surrounding countryside through the stories of travellers who had passed through the Bent Needle, the reality proved somewhat less impressive. Famous trees were smaller than expected. Great rocks were merely rocks. Nevertheless, Dean remained determined to appreciate each landmark, no matter how disappointing it might be in person.
As daylight faded, the party brought their cart to a stop and established their first camp. Ash began gathering herbs, moss and other useful materials from the nearby wilderness, while Flint collected enough firewood to see them through the evening. Dean prepared a substantial stew, momentarily forgetting that neither Flint nor Hemlock required food and leaving Ash as the only person capable of helping him finish it.
With camp established and the horses secured as competently as the party could manage, Flynn entered his standby state before taking watch over the others.
Some time later, he heard movement amongst the trees. At first, it appeared to be nothing more than an animal passing through the undergrowth. Then Flint saw a larger silhouette moving along the road. He woke Dean.
Looking into the darkness, Dean saw a heavily robed figure approaching the camp. The stranger was completely covered in mismatched layers of cloth, with only a pair of faded blue eyes visible beneath the wrappings. A large shield rested across his back, a sword hung at his side and the sound of metal beneath the robes suggested that he was wearing armour.
Ash slipped quietly from the cart and circled into the trees while Dean confronted the stranger directly. The figure claimed to be searching for a companion. His voice sounded familiar.
After several tense questions, it became increasingly clear that the stranger was searching for Vadim. The party told him what had happened at Belcons Manor and explained that Vadim had been cremated according to his final wishes. When shown Vadim’s locket, the stranger opened it and stared at the two figures within. He then introduced himself. His name was Aleksander. Vadim had been his son.
The party explained how Vadim had fought beside them, protected the people of Needleberry and ultimately sacrificed himself during the battle at Belcons Manor. Aleksander listened quietly. Though he had arrived too late to find his son alive, the party assured him that Vadim had not died alone. He had been surrounded by people who valued him, even if he had spent much of their short time together stubbornly refusing medical attention.
Before the conversation could continue, a scream echoed from somewhere within the forest. The party immediately followed the sound. They emerged into a clearing containing a small camp belonging to refugees from the nearby settlement of Canterbury. Several frightened survivors stood huddled together while a familiar pale creature fed upon a body at their feet.
It was another vampire thrall. Unlike those encountered beneath Needleberry, this creature appeared well-fed. Its body was less withered, its movements stronger and its attention immediately turned towards the newcomers.
Ash charged forward and struck it with an alchemical mixture of fire and vitality. The attack burned into the creature, but also drew its attention away from the refugees. It retaliated with terrifying speed. A single blow knocked Ash unconscious.
Dean rushed forward and used his magic to protect and stabilise Ash while Flint attempted to exploit the creature’s supernatural vulnerabilities. Aleksander advanced behind them, shield raised, and seized the thrall before it could reach the remaining refugees.
As Aleksander grappled with the creature, he pulled the cloth away from his mouth. Fangs extended from beneath his lips. He attempted to bite the thrall. Despite the sudden revelation, the party continued their attack. Ash regained consciousness and hurled another alchemical concoction, weakening the creature against acid, fire and slashing weapons. Dean’s magic protected Aleksander as he held it in place, allowing Flint to close the distance.
With the creature trapped in Alexander’s grasp, Flint struck. His blade tore through its throat, severing its head and sending it rolling from Aleksander’s arms. The creature collapsed and began to burn away into ash.
Three of the Canterbury refugees remained alive. They explained that creatures like this one had attacked their settlement several nights earlier and killed most of its population. The survivors had fled south, seeking whatever safety they could find.
The party helped them gather their belongings and warned them that the bodies of the dead would need to be burned before they could rise again. Dean offered the survivors what remained of the evening’s stew and told them to travel towards Needleberry. The Bent Needle had been left in the care of the community and would provide them with shelter.
The survivors accepted, though their gratitude became noticeably more cautious once they realised the party was now travelling with a vampire. The following morning, the two groups separated. The refugees began their journey towards Needleberry while the party continued north.
During the journey, Aleksander finally explained what he was. Before becoming a vampire, he and his wife Nadine had worked as monster hunters. They guarded travellers, protected settlements and removed dangerous creatures from places where ordinary people could not defend themselves.
Their final contract led them to a mansion in the north. The person who had hired them was not its victim, but its master. Malcorvus. Alexander and Elara were captured. Alexander was drained and transformed, while Elara  made an agreement to protect their son. She would serve Malcorvus if Vadim was allowed to live.
Malcovbus kept his word only in the cruellest possible manner. Vadim survived, but was forced to witness what his parents had become. Elara remained under Malcorvus’ control, while Aleksander was imprisoned and tortured until he eventually escaped. By the time Aleksander returned, the mansion had been abandoned. Elara, Vadim and Malcorvus were gone. Alexander had been searching for them ever since.
Unlike the thralls the party had encountered, Aleksander retained his independence. He claimed that greater vampires could exert control over those beneath them, but he had somehow broken free of Malcorvus’ influence. He still required blood, though he insisted that he did not kill those he fed upon.
He also shared what he knew of vampire weaknesses. Sunlight was dangerous to them, as were fire and forms of vitality magic intended to harm the undead. Older vampires were generally more powerful, and many lesser vampires remained bound to the will of those who created them. With Vadim dead and vampires apparently responsible for it, Aleksander’s path now led in the same direction as the party’s. North.
The discussion eventually turned towards Flint and his strange connection to the vampire creatures. When Dwarven commands were spoken around him, Flint reacted automatically, declaring that his obedience protocols had been disengaged. The response unsettled Alexander, who recognised something in it resembling the supernatural domination used by powerful vampires.
Ash offered to investigate Flynn’s internal mechanisms. The cart was brought to a stop and Flint allowed Ash to open one of the panels along his back. Ash had barely begun examining the unfamiliar machinery when a violent surge of electricity erupted from inside Flint’s body.
Ash was thrown across the road and into a nearby tree. The shock was powerful enough to knock him unconscious and warp the screwdriver still clenched in his hand. Dean used his magic to restore him, although Ash remained dazed and barely responsive for some time afterwards.
As the party resumed their journey, Flint suddenly stood rigidly upright. His eyes turned red. He began speaking in harsh, guttural Dwarven. Then, just as quickly, his eyes returned to normal and his body relaxed. Flint appeared to have no memory of what had happened.
Whatever existed within him was not merely damaged machinery. Something remained connected to his past, and potentially to whatever awaited them in the north. The party continued along the road towards the small settlement of Waymeet. Beyond it lay Ironwall, the Stonewood Spine and the mysteries drawing each of them forward. Four days of wilderness travel still remained.

session-recaps/pc---session-8.title: PC - Session 8
session-recaps/pc---session-8.content:
The party continued north towards PC - Waymeet, travelling through increasingly empty winter country.
After several days on the road, they encountered two brothers, Tobias and Edwin Marrick. The Marricks are travelling cartographers and self-described “story-finders” who collect old maps, wartime accounts, local legends and stories of places that have disappeared from modern maps.
The party agreed to escort them safely to Waymeet. In return, the Marricks promised to add several unusual locations around the PC - The Stoneward Spine to the party’s map, each associated with rumours of something interesting or valuable.
The brothers also spoke about the growing danger of the northern roads. While dwarven rule over the Stoneward Spine was hardly remembered fondly, their control of the mountains had kept many dangerous creatures contained. Since the end of that rule, travellers have increasingly reported creatures wandering further from the Spine.
Feeding Aleksander
With PC - Aleksander needing blood, Dean volunteered rather than risk another traveller becoming his meal.
Under Ash’s supervision, Aleksander fed from Dean without seriously harming him, establishing that he can feed from a willing person without killing them.
It also gave Dean his  first proper look beneath Aleksander’s wrappings: an older, deathly pale man with white hair and grey eyes.
The following morning, a hungover Dean awoke to discover Ash attempting to cook breakfast with the precision of an alchemist and none of the instincts of a cook.
Meanwhile, PC - Flint went looking for eggs and instead returned with a rather dangerous alchemical root.
The Spider
Later that day, the party found a deliberately felled tree blocking the road. A discarded crossbow, scattered coins and traces of frozen blood suggested an ambush, although there were no bodies.
While investigating, Ash discovered the real threat when a giant trapdoor spider erupted from beneath the snow.
Flint was badly poisoned and briefly went down during the fight, but Dean kept him alive while Ash weakened the creature. Aleksander eventually finished it by driving his sword through its head.
The spider’s burrow revealed that the apparent bandits had themselves become its victims. Among their remaining possessions, the party recovered coin, healing supplies, a silver dagger, jewellery and other equipment.
More unusually, they found a heavy iron token stamped:
HOLT CONSOLIDATED On one side
37 on the other
The Marricks recognised Holt Consolidated as an organisation connected to PC - Ironwall, although the significance of the token remains unknown.
With the spider dead and the road ahead cleared, the party continued towards PC - Waymeet.
The Marricks still owe them the map locations

session-recaps/pc---session-2.title: Pc - Session 2
session-recaps/pc---session-2.content:
The growl echoed across Needleberry.
As the party looked towards the centre of town, more of the creatures began to emerge from the streets and alleyways. They did not hunt. They gathered. One by one they turned towards the same point somewhere within the storm, moving with an unsettling discipline that felt more like soldiers than monsters.
Then the blizzard returned with full force.
The wind howled through the streets, swallowing the town beneath sheets of snow. Through the storm, the party caught only a brief glimpse of two crimson eyes watching from a rooftop before both the figure and its followers disappeared into the white.
With the cold becoming just as deadly as the creatures themselves, Bromm Hartwell called the party into the safety of his smithy.
Before joining the others, Dean noticed movement outside The Pincushion.
He found Edda Voss buried beneath the snow, her life already slipping away. Despite everything that had happened, her final thoughts remained with the town, speaking only briefly before passing away in Dean’s arms.
The party spent the night sheltering inside the smithy as the storm raged outside. They spoke long into the evening, taking stock of everything they had witnessed. Ash warned of the dangers surrounding the occult and spoke of Malach Vey, whilst the others shared what little they understood of the creatures. Questions continued to outnumber answers.
Morning brought no relief. The storm had buried much of Needleberry beneath deep snowdrifts. After digging their way from the smithy, the party found the town already at work clearing roads, repairing buildings and accounting for those who had survived.
Soon afterwards they were summoned to the Town Hall. There, Irilard Belcons addressed the surviving townsfolk. Seven people had been lost during the night, and the creatures would almost certainly return. The town would prepare itself for another attack.
When the party revealed they had successfully killed one of the creatures, Belcons entrusted them with a task no one else could undertake. Find where they came from.
The investigation began by speaking with Mary Whittaker, the oldest resident they could find, in the hope she had heard stories of similar events.
Then to The Pincushion, where the party gathered what supplies remained to use against the creatures. Their search also took them through the graveyard before they eventually turned their attention towards the abandoned Needleworks.
Inside, they discovered the body of another victim hidden within an upstairs cupboard, bearing the same puncture wounds seen elsewhere throughout the town. Careful investigation revealed marks where one of the creatures had leapt through an upstairs window before disappearing into the surrounding forest.
Following the trail proved difficult beneath the fresh snow. Vadim eventually lost the tracks, though, without realising it, Flint slowly drifted to the front of the group and continued leading them in the correct direction before eventually stopping, seemingly unaware that he had done so. Ash and Dean soon rediscovered the trail, eventually leading the party to the entrance of an abandoned cave hidden amongst the hills beyond Needleberry.
Deep within the cave they found the remnants of an old camp, untouched for decades.
And amongst it, the creatures.
They stood perfectly still, eyes closed, waiting in complete silence. As the party turned to sneak out, a voice echoed through the darkness.
”…Persistence… unexpected…”
”…Will… still… persists…”
”…Incomplete…”
”…Custodian…”
As the final word faded, every creature opened its eyes. The party fled. Realising they could never outrun them through the tunnels, Dean spotted a boarded-up passage leading into a smaller chamber. They forced their way through just as the creatures closed the distance behind them.
Vadim narrowly escaped being overwhelmed before the wooden structure above the passage was brought crashing down, sealing most of the creatures behind it.
Only two made it through. Using a pair of mirrors to direct shafts of sunlight around the chamber, the party discovered the creatures’ greatest weakness. Blinded by the light, one fell quickly before the others could break through the collapsing barricade.
With the sounds of more creatures drawing ever closer, the party climbed the ladder towards the surface, emerging into the winter daylight as the creatures below remained trapped beneath the mountain, unable to follow into the sun.
